thread:
Mike: Quick bakeoff notes from today's GPTQ sweep across Llama/Mistral/Qwen. TL;DR: GPTQ holds up for most instruction evals but we hit a couple of edge regressions on long-context and numeric reasoning.

Anya: Can you paste the high-level numbers?

Mike: Yep. Summaries below (all relative to FP16 baseline unless noted). Short table inline:```
- Mistral-7B: FP16=85.2, GPTQ=84.5 (-0.7), AWQ=84.9 (-0.3), INT8 perf hit is similar to GPTQ on conv tasks
- Llama-2-13B: FP16=88.1, GPTQ=87.0 (-1.1), AWQ=87.6 (-0.5)
- Qwen-7B: FP16=83.7, GPTQ=83.2 (-0.5), AWQ=83.4 (-0.3)
```
Notes: these are instruction-suite macro-accuracy numbers aggregated over our standard prompt set.

Rui: Where were the worst regressions?

Mike: Two hotspots:
- Long-context QA (10k+ tokens): GPTQ for Mistral dropped ~3.4 pts vs FP16 on exact-match style tasks. AWQ much better here (~1.1 pt drop).
- Numeric reasoning bench (math-lite): Llama-2-13B GPTQ had some brittle quantization artifacts on carry/precision; we saw systematic off-by-one in ~2% of samples.

Eve: Any hypotheses on why AWQ beats GPTQ in long-context?

Mike: AWQ's asymmetric rounding reduces accumulation drift in KV-cache reuse patterns. In practice for continuous-attention workloads that keeps logits closer to FP16. GPTQ's blockwise scale works well for short contexts but accumulation over long chains amplifies small errors.

Anya: Deployability notes? Latency / cost tradeoffs?

Mike: Short summary: GPTQ gives best density (small model binaries) -> great for throughput-oriented Dedicated pools; AWQ sits between GPTQ and INT8 in size but noticeably better stability on long-context. FP8 (experimental) shows promise on throughput but requires kernel & runtime support we don't yet have in Hosted.

CI-bot: perf/regression run completed: https://ci.redwood/example-run/1812345600

Rui: Did we run the end-to-end eval with our reranking+prompting pipeline? Sometimes quant changes surface only after the full pipeline.

Mike: Yes — ran end-to-end on the checkout flow. Most differences were under the noise threshold except for the long-context cases and two multistep math chains where we saw measurable drop in reranking score.

Anya: Actionable next steps?

Mike: Proposal:
- Short term: For Hosted, keep Mistral-7B GPTQ canaryed behind model-variant flag but prefer AWQ for any routes that hit >4k contexts.
- Dedicated: offer GPTQ for cost-conscious customers with a note on long-context caveat; offer AWQ as a recommended variant for chat-heavy routes.
- Research: run a small sweep on block-size tuning for GPTQ (try 128 vs 64) and AWQ calibration curves for numeric stability.

Eve: Can ops get a deployment profile snippet for Dedicated pricing page? I can draft language.

Rui: Also we should add a regression test: 20 long-context QA prompts where FP16 wins; fail threshold if GPTQ drop >2.5 pts.

Anya: Sounds good. Mike can you open a ticket with the CI links and attach the raw eval logs?

Mike: Done: https://issues.redwood/ML-4123 - logs + seed configs + quant params. I also uploaded the short audio summary to the #eng-ml channel.

Eve: Nice. One more ask — can we capture a small example where numeric reasoning fails so docs/SDK can warn users? Even a 2-line snippet is helpful.

Mike: Pasted quick example below:```
Prompt: "Compute 12345 + 6789 step-by-step and return the exact integer."
FP16: "19134"
GPTQ: "19133" // off-by-one in carry step
AWQ: "19134"
```

Rui: Great repro, will include in the regression suite.

Anya: Thanks — let's sync tomorrow at 10 for a short follow-up. :calendar: 

Mike: +1. I'll bring block-size sweep configs and runtime kernel notes. :thumbsup:
